column1: # The Wena desktop - the native Nuklear GUI - for every platform it is built for.
# Every target is one self-contained release file: everything it needs is linked
# in, including the licenses of what is (`wena --licenses`). Each is built by one
# job of .github/workflows/release-all.yml, the only release workflow.
#   linux    in a container of that CPU, native or under QEMU (scripts/build_desktop_release_container.sh)
#   bsd      in a virtual machine of that system (scripts/build_desktop_release_vm.sh)
#   windows  cross-compiled with MinGW-w64 on Linux, then run on a Windows runner
#   amiga    in that system's cross-compiler container (scripts/build_desktop_amiga.sh)
#   android  with the Android NDK and SDK (scripts/build_desktop_android.sh)
#   ios      with Xcode on a macOS runner (scripts/build_desktop_ios.sh)
# planned: freebsd-riscv64 - FreeBSD publishes no riscv64 packages (pkg.freebsd.org has
#   no FreeBSD:14 or :15 riscv64 repository), so its VM has no Python, make or X11;
#   the way there is cross-compiling from Linux against its base and X11 headers.
# AROS, one file per CPU, named for the CPU as every other target is: aros-amd64
#   is the x86-64 ABI (it was once misnamed aros-x86), aros-i386 the 32-bit ABIv0
#   line of deadwood2/AROS. AROS on m68k runs AmigaOS 3 executables, so it uses
#   wena-amigaos-m68k; AROS on ARM has no published toolchain or SDK to build with.
